findings.symptom: First resize drag on a no-width (stretch) column anchors to the 120px fallback instead of the rendered 200px: 80px pointer dead zone with zero visual response; commit = 120+Δ not renderedWidth+Δ (+90px drag grows +10px); negative drags are visually swallowed entirely while a bogus tracked width is committed
findings.evidence: mid-drag readings at +10..+80px: th/col width stays 200; +90px → 210; +120px → 240; negative -40/-60px: rendered stays 200 (w-full auto layout restores); once a width is tracked (240), subsequent drags are exact (240+60=300)
findings.ownership: renderer: packages/flux-renderers-data/src/table-renderer/use-column-resize.ts startWidth = widths[key] ?? resolveColumnWidth(column) (120 fallback) disconnected from measured colgroup width (column-width-measure.ts)
findings.redE2e: read Name col width W; drag handle +40px → assert mid-drag and committed width = W+40 (currently stays W); drag -40 → assert W-40 (currently W)

findings.symptom: Column resize has no cancel path: Esc mid-drag ignored (drag continues and commits), pointercancel runs the same commit path as pointerup, double-click does not reset
findings.evidence: Esc mid-drag then release: width 210→290 (committed through Esc); synthetic pointercancel mid-drag: 310→360 (+50 committed); dblclick on handle: 360→360 no-op; use-column-resize.ts:337-338 binds pointerup and pointercancel to the same finish
findings.redE2e: pointerdown → move +50 → pointercancel → assert width unchanged (currently +50 → red)
